format: full-bleed image + one line on-slide; narration in presenter notes
emotional_spine: He is both merciful and just — the cross is where mercy and justice meet

beats.line: WHY SUFFERING?
If God is good — why is the world like this?
beats.subject: A lone human figure standing in a ruined, sorrowful landscape at dusk — a person bowed under grief amid the brokenness of the world (distant rubble, a bare tree, gathering shadow), yet a faint thread of warm light breaks through the heavy clouds above them. The ache of the problem of evil, rendered with compassion and dignity, not despair. The light is small but present.

beats.line: The answer is older than you are.
Before us, a universe at peace.
beats.subject: A vast, luminous heavenly realm filled with ranks of radiant angelic beings in serene harmony, bathed in warm golden light, gathered before a distant glorious throne. Peace, joy, perfect order. No shadow anywhere. The host of heaven worshipping in unity before sin existed.

beats.line: And one stood highest of all.
He guarded one thing: the law of love.
Heaven had a blueprint on earth.
Two angels, wings spread, covering the law.
Because God is love.
beats.scene: the heart of God / radiant love
beats.subject: A warm, overwhelming radiance of divine love emanating from a heavenly source — golden light pouring outward like an embrace, soft and tender rather than blinding, suggesting the very heart of God. Abstract-leaning but warm and personal; the feeling of being loved. Glowing, intimate, awe-filled.

beats.line: And love can never be forced.
Then the highest heart turned.
beats.subject: The same magnificent covering angel, but now a subtle shadow crossing his beautiful face — pride and self-admiration dawning in his eyes as he gazes at his own glory rather than the throne. Still radiant and beautiful, but the first hint of darkness, a coldness entering. The tragedy of the highest being beginning to fall. Painterly, somber undertone beneath the gold.

beats.line: “The law must be wrong.”
beats.subject: A dark, dramatic moment in heaven — the once-radiant angel now turning away from the throne's light, a storm of shadow beginning to gather around him as other angelic figures look on in dismay. The light still shines behind him but he casts a long shadow. The birth of rebellion and accusation. Tension between the golden glory and the encroaching dark.

beats.line: Love cannot answer a lie with a sword.
beats.subject: A vast heavenly throne in radiant glory, and before it the watching host of angels — a sense of a terrible choice held in restraint, mercy staying the hand of power. The light does not strike; it waits. Solemn, weighty, full of restrained love. The throne could destroy but chooses not to.

beats.line: A charge like this can only be disproven — in the open.
beats.subject: An immense, awe-inspiring heavenly courtroom or judgment hall stretching into golden infinity, ranks of angelic witnesses arrayed on either side, a luminous throne at the far end. The sense of a great trial about to be heard before the whole universe. Majestic, vast, reverent.

beats.line: So He made you. To see for yourself.
The first morning of the world.
beats.subject: The dawn of Eden — a lush, pristine garden paradise at golden sunrise, two human figures (a man and a woman) standing small in wonder amid abundant beauty, rivers and trees, soft divine light blessing the scene. The innocence and joy of the first morning. Warm, hopeful, idyllic.

beats.line: Justice let the other side speak too.
beats.subject: A single striking tree in the center of a beautiful garden, dappled with light and a faint shadow, set apart and significant — the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Beautiful but charged with meaning, a serpent's coil barely visible in its branches. The one place the accuser could make his case. Lush but with an undercurrent of tension.

beats.line: And we believed the accuser.
beats.subject: The moment of the fall in Eden — the woman and man having taken the fruit, the garden's golden light beginning to dim and cool around them, the first shadow of guilt and loss on their faces as they realize what they've done. Sorrowful, the warmth draining toward grey. The turning point of the world. Tender and tragic, not lurid.

beats.line: The accuser thought he had won a world.
beats.subject: A dark, brooding figure (the adversary) standing triumphant over a now-shadowed earth, the globe beneath a sky turned stormy and grey, his form silhouetted against a cold light — believing he has seized a kingdom. Ominous, the warm gold now mostly eclipsed by shadow. Power apparently won, but hollow.

beats.line: He did not know the love of God.
beats.subject: The Father and the Son together in heavenly glory, heads bowed close in a moment of profound shared resolve and sorrowful love — a covenant of sacrifice being made, warm light surrounding them, the weight of a costly decision. Intimate, tender, the love between Father and Son radiant. The plan to save us conceived in love.

beats.line: Two paths that look the same — until they don't.
He let the world groan — so it would never groan again.
beats.subject: A weary, suffering world under a heavy sky — distant human struggle and a creation in travail — yet held within a faint, vast, encircling presence of light at the edges of the frame, as if cradled. Sorrow and patience together. The long ache of history, but not abandoned. Somber gold and grey.

beats.line: And He did not watch from a safe distance.
beats.scene: God enters the suffering / Jesus weeps
beats.subject: Jesus of Nazareth, first-century Jewish man with olive-brown skin and a beard, weeping — tears on his face, his expression full of compassion and grief, standing among the sorrowing. Tender, deeply human, divine love entering human pain. Close, intimate, warm light on his face. (Match the Jesus depiction style of the Day-2 deck.)

beats.line: Justice and mercy — pick one, God.
beats.subject: A symbolic image of a balance or scales held in tension under a dramatic sky — justice and mercy seemingly opposed, a heavy moral weight, divine light straining between two demands. Solemn, weighty, the cross faintly foreshadowed in the composition's crossing lines. Dramatic chiaroscuro.

beats.line: He did not waive the law. He paid it.
beats.subject: The crucifixion at Calvary — the cross raised against a dark, dramatic sky torn with a break of divine light, the figure of Christ upon it, the moment of ultimate sacrifice. Reverent, awe-filled, sorrowful but glorious. Warm light breaking through the storm. Not graphic or gory — dignified, painterly, the weight of love. (Match the Day-2 Jesus/biblical scene style.)

beats.line: And the accuser was unmasked before the universe.
beats.scene: the accuser exposed at the cross
beats.subject: The cross on the hill of Calvary seen from a cosmic vantage, brilliant divine light radiating from it across the heavens, and the shadow of the adversary recoiling and shrinking away into darkness, defeated and exposed before a watching universe of light. The triumph of the cross over the accuser. Epic, redemptive, the gold overwhelming the shadow.

beats.line: At the cross, mercy and justice met — and kissed.
beats.subject: A radiant, reconciling image — the scales of justice and a gesture of mercy united and at peace under the light of the cross, the two former opposites now harmonized in golden glory. Resolution, peace, the heart of the night. Warm, luminous, the storm passed. (Psalm 85:10 — mercy and truth met together, righteousness and peace kissed.)

beats.line: None of us could ever earn this.
beats.subject: A humble human figure kneeling in soft light, hands open and empty, receiving rather than achieving — bathed in gentle warm radiance from above, a posture of grace received as a gift. Tender, humble, hopeful. The relief of grace, not the weight of judgment. Intimate.

beats.line: The same cross that cleared His name — reopens your way home.
He will wipe away every tear.
beats.subject: The restored new earth — a radiant paradise at golden dawn, lush and whole, a great city of light glowing in the distance, redeemed people walking in joy and peace amid abundant beauty, no more shadow. The reversal of all suffering. Glorious, hopeful, overwhelmingly warm and bright. The home we were made for.

beats.line: And suffering will never rise again.
beats.scene: affliction will not rise a second time
beats.subject: A serene, eternal heavenly vista of perfect peace — the throne of God and of the Lamb at the center radiating gentle light over a healed creation, no darkness anywhere, a sense of forever-safety and rest. Calm, complete, secure. The final peace of the universe. Warm and still.

beats.line: He stands at the door, and knocks.
Your move.
beats.subject: Jesus, first-century Jewish man with olive-brown skin and a beard, standing with a hand extended warmly toward the viewer in gentle invitation, his face full of love and welcome, bathed in soft golden light. Personal, inviting, tender — the final appeal. The Savior reaching out to you. (Match the Day-2 Jesus depiction style.)
